units: Fixed L0, E0 and mass M0; time t0=sqrt(M0*L0^2/E0). Variables below are their dimensionless numerical values. Temperature means kB*Tphysical/E0.
apparatus: Five identical classical point scatterers have known trap centers x_j=j for j=0,...,4 and scalar displacement u_j along the line. Their masses equal1. The ideal potential is K/2 times [.6*sum_j u_j^2 + coupling*sum_{j=0}^3(u_(j+1)-u_j)^2]. There is no periodic closing link, excluded volume or other interaction. K is one common unknown in [.8,1.2].

At all times each momentum obeys dp_j=[-partial U/partial u_j-.4*p_j]dt+sqrt(.8*T)dW_j and du_j=p_j dt, with independent standard Wiener increments. Before observation the complete array is in the stationary classical Gibbs state at the prescribed T. The local bath remains active during the observation. Pinning removes the translation zero mode.

A negligibly weak single-scattering optical probe sees identical known scalar scattering amplitudes. An ideal phase-stable heterodyne reference separately records both quadratures of the scattered complex field. After removal of the known single-scatterer gain and carrier phase, its amplitude is A_q(t)=sum_j exp[i*q*(j+u_j(t))]/sqrt(5).

The reported value is the real part of the ensemble cross correlation of the recorded complex field at delay t and its conjugate at time0. It includes the mean field. It is not an intensity-intensity correlation or an inferred correlation from a Siegert relation. The probe has no appreciable mechanical force or heating.
calibration_outline: Equal-time q=2*pi records with coupling1 at three temperatures, together with nonzero delays .3 and .8 at coupling0, give9 distinct settings. No noisy data or hidden grader exists yet.
readout_normalization: Dimensionless real field correlation per scatterer; no division by a vanishing contrast or individual hidden signal.
